title: Understanding SVD
text: The singular value decomposition (SVD) of a matrix X is given by X=U*S*V**T. Here, U and V are orthogonal matrices, and S is a diagonal matrix with non-negative real numbers on the diagonal.

title: Properties of V
text: The columns of V are the right singular vectors of X. They are orthogonal and represent the directions of maximum variance in the data.

title: Direction of Maximum Variance
text: The first column of V corresponds to the direction of maximum variance in the data. This is because the singular values in S are sorted in descending order, and the first singular value corresponds to the largest variance.
